issue_294_text: planner identifies a unit completely solvable/verifiable by an existing/new deterministic mechanism and does not spend an unnecessary reasoning-worker call on that unit
status: not exercised -- no real #294 occurrence exists, and two rounds of constructing a synthetic worker-unit contract to substitute for one were themselves found invalid (Stage 2 audit #400)
why_the_original_demonstration_no_longer: The original version of this proof-run pointed at real #294 units 294-B and 294-C, whose own 'Files/surfaces expected to change' fields name the very scripts each unit was itself building (parse-execution-plan.mjs and prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs respectively).

Stage 2 post-merge audit #396 correctly found that this was never actually the right example for this scenario: 'deterministic route' in #294's own Verification section describes routing a unit to a genuine PRE-EXISTING mechanism it merely invokes, not a script the unit is itself producing.

PR #393's Stage 1 fix added `isUnitsOwnDeliverable` to tools/orchestration/prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs's `resolveUnitRoute`, correctly excluding a script named in a unit's own 'Required bounded outcome' field from the deterministic-script route even when it is also named in 'Files/surfaces expected to change'. Post-fix, 294-B and 294-C no longer route to their own deliverable scripts -- see the refreshed live re-run below -- so they no longer demonstrate this scenario at all.

No real unit in #294's own history has a 'Files/surfaces expected to change' field naming a pre-existing script that is genuinely NOT that unit's own deliverable -- every real unit in this plan built the scripts it named -- so no real live #294 occurrence exists to substitute.

refreshed_live_rerun.description: Re-running the real, now-fixed prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs against the real live #294 plan, after all fixes to date (PR #393's isUnitsOwnDeliverable fix, PR #399's extractCapabilityClassLabel sentence-boundary fix and its own abbreviation-safety hardening).
refreshed_live_rerun.interpretation: 294-B and 294-C now correctly fall through to the capability-class table ('bounded implementation worker') instead of the deterministic-script route, because their own 'Files/surfaces expected to change' scripts are also named as their own deliverables in 'Required bounded outcome'. This remains genuine, valid evidence that the own-deliverable exclusion (PR #393's fix) works correctly against real live plan state -- it is NOT evidence for this scenario's own positive claim (routing to a genuine pre-existing mechanism), which is a different, unproven claim -- see the abandoned constructed-exercise history below.

constructed_exercise_history_abandoned.description: Two rounds of constructing a synthetic worker-unit contract to substitute for a real #294 occurrence were attempted and committed (docs/execution-planning-proof-runs/294-scenario-04-deterministic-route-exercise.mjs, since deleted), each fixing the prior round's own defect, before Stage 2 audit #400 found the underlying approach itself unsound rather than merely mis-executed:
constructed_exercise_history_abandoned.round_1_defect: The first synthetic unit's 'Required bounded outcome' required producing a second, unrelated documentation deliverable that the invoked gate script (ready-dispatch-gate.mjs) cannot produce -- a false-positive route that left the unit's real outcome unfinished (Stage 1 review finding on PR #399).
constructed_exercise_history_abandoned.round_2_defect_and_stop: The second version removed the unrelated deliverable but still named the invoked script in 'Files/surfaces expected to change' while separately asserting in prose that the script was 'not modified' -- an internally contradictory worker-unit contract, since that field's own name ('expected to change') asserts the opposite of what the prose claims (Stage 2 audit #400, P1). Codex's own audit correctly identified that the current fixed 13-field Worker Unit Contract schema (per #294's Shared Contract v1) has no field that can truthfully express 'this unit's work invokes an existing script without modifying it' -- 'Files/surfaces expected to change' is definitionally about files that DO change, and no synthetic unit can honestly claim a pre-existing, unmodified script belongs there. Rather than attempt a third synthetic contrivance against a schema that cannot truthfully express this case, this scenario is recorded honestly as not exercised, matching the established honesty precedent already used for scenarios 5, 7, and 10 in this same document -- fabricating a result against an admittedly-inadequate schema would repeat exactly the overstatement audit #400 flagged.

schema_gap_noted_for_future_work: Whether the real, shipped mechanism (resolveUnitRoute) correctly routes a unit to a genuine pre-existing mechanism it merely invokes (as opposed to its own deliverable) remains formally unverified, because no valid worker-unit contract -- real or synthetic -- currently exists to exercise it. This is a genuine gap in the Worker Unit Contract schema (no field distinguishes 'invokes an existing mechanism without modifying it' from 'files this unit's own work changes'), not a code defect in resolveUnitRoute itself. Addressing it (e.g. a new field, or documented conventions for the existing fields) is future work, out of scope for this correction round.
honest_caveat: This scenario is NOT demonstrated -- neither by a real, naturally-occurring #294 unit (none exists; every real unit built the script it named), nor by a constructed synthetic unit (two attempts were made and committed, and both were found invalid on independent review; see constructed_exercise_history_abandoned above). The refreshed live re-run shows the real mechanism, now correctly fixed, no longer misroutes 294-B/294-C to their own deliverables -- genuine, valid evidence for that fix specifically -- but that is a different claim from this scenario's own positive claim about routing to a genuine pre-existing mechanism, which remains unverified. This status was downgraded twice: first from 'demonstrated' (audit #396 found the original real-world example was the wrong example), then from 'demonstrated via constructed exercise' to 'not exercised' (audit #400 found the constructed exercise itself invalid). See schema_gap_noted_for_future_work above for why a third synthetic attempt was not made.
